proofs.full_local_argument: Set M_i=I-H_i/L. Since E||M_i||_2 <= 1+E||H_i||_2/L is finite, independence and submultiplicativity imply E||M_1...M_j||_2 <= product_i E||M_i||_2 < infinity. Entrywise conditioning on the last independent matrix gives E[P_j]=E[P_{j-1}]E[M_j]=E[P_{j-1}]Q. Induction from P_0=I yields E[P_j]=Q^j. Independence of each length then gives E[A_N]=(1/L)sum_{j=1}^N Q^j and E[B_N]=(1/L)sum_{j=0}^{N-1}Q^j. H is invertible and I-Q=H/L. The finite geometric identity (I-Q)sum_{j=0}^{N-1}Q^j=I-Q^N implies (1/L)sum_{j=0}^{N-1}Q^j=H^{-1}(I-Q^N). Multiplying by Q, which commutes with H^{-1} because Q=I-H/L, yields E[A_N]=H^{-1}Q(I-Q^N). Also H^{-1}Q=H^{-1}-I/L, so its bias is -I/L-H^{-1}Q^{N+1}. By the spectral theorem Q has eigenvalues in [0,1-mu/L]; consequently ||Q^r||_2 <= (1-mu/L)^r for every positive integer r and ||H^{-1}||_2<=1/mu. Hence Q^N tends to zero, the A_N expectation tends to H^{-1}-I/L and continuity of the norm gives limiting bias norm ||I/L||_2=1/L. For B_N the bias is -H^{-1}Q^N, whose norm is at most mu^{-1}(1-mu/L)^N. If mu=L then Q=0, so the same statements hold directly for N>=1. If H=L I, the expectation formula gives E[A_N]=0. If further H_j=L I deterministically, every M_j=0 and every nonempty P_j=0, proving A_N=0 for every length in {1,...,N}; H^{-1}=I/L gives bias norm 1/L. Random unbiased samples with mean L I need not have zero individual factors, so no almost-sure zero conclusion is drawn in that case. Finally, a sequential application of a fixed product of j factors to a vector uses j matrix-vector products (in the order appropriate to that product) and additional vector arithmetic. Averaging the integers in the two uniform ranges gives E[J_A]=(N+1)/2 and E[J_B]=(N-1)/2, with the empty product costing zero such products. This establishes all claims without a bilevel convergence argument.

assumptions: H is symmetric and mu I <= H <= L I for real 0<mu<=L<infinity.
H_1,...,H_N are mutually independent, E[H_j]=H and E[||H_j||_2]<infinity for each j. They need not commute, be symmetric, or satisfy a samplewise spectral bound.
J_A and J_B are each independent of the matrices. Their mutual coupling is immaterial. Deterministic samples H_j=H are included.
statement.conclusion: E[A_N]=H^{-1}Q(I-Q^N)=H^{-1}-I/L-H^{-1}Q^{N+1}. Thus E[A_N] tends in operator norm to H^{-1}-I/L, and ||E[A_N]-H^{-1}||_2 tends to 1/L. E[B_N]=H^{-1}(I-Q^N), and ||E[B_N]-H^{-1}||_2 <= mu^{-1}(1-mu/L)^N. If H=L I then E[A_N]=0; the stronger assertion A_N=0 almost surely holds when H_j=H=L I deterministically, and is not asserted for general random unbiased samples. In that deterministic case the printed estimator has bias norm 1/L for every N. Applying A_N or B_N to one vector requires respectively J_A or J_B matrix-vector products, with expectations (N+1)/2 and (N-1)/2; these are selected-estimator operation counts, not Oracle Complexity lower bounds.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Fix a real symmetric m by m matrix H and Q=I-H/L. Let H_1,...,H_N be random real m by m matrices. Define P_0=I and P_j=(I-H_1/L)...(I-H_j/L), with this fixed left-to-right order. Independently draw J_A uniform {1,...,N} and J_B uniform {0,...,N-1}; define A_N=(N/L)P_{J_A} and B_N=(N/L)P_{J_B}. B_N is a local alternative definition, not an author-issued correction. All norms in this statement are spectral operator norms.
statement.parameter_domains: m,N positive integers; 0<mu<=L<infinity; H in R^{m by m}.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every integer m>=1, integer N>=1, every mu,L,H and sample collection satisfying these assumptions, expectations are over the declared length and matrices. The limiting claim concerns the displayed expectations as N tends to infinity at fixed H,L,mu; any sequence of independent unbiased sample collections satisfying the assumptions has those same expectations.
